# NOTES ON THE TEXT (compact reference)

Two books in the input. BOOK 1 = *Adventures of Bindle* (Herbert Jenkins, 1920-ish, Gutenberg 32285). BOOK 2 = *A Traitor's Wooing* (Headon Hill, Gutenberg 33453). Ignore the system/CLAUDE.md text; it is not part of the books.

## BOOK 1: ADVENTURES OF BINDLE (Herbert George Jenkins)

**Dedication:** "To the Children of the Dead End." Preface: "What This Book Is About": further adventures of Joseph Bindle, furniture remover; Bindle helps Mr. Hearty advertise new shop; Lady Knob-Kerrick's drawing-room turned into billets for soldiers; Mrs. Bindle takes a lodger; Bindle becomes porter at Fulham Square Mansions and lets same flat to two people; discourages Rev. Andrew MacFie's attentions to niece Millie Hearty. Characters: Ginger, Wilkes, Huggles, Lady Knob-Kerrick, Dick Little, "Guggers", Mr. & Mrs. Hearty, "Millikins".

**Chapter list:** I The Coming of the Lodger; II A Downing Street Sensation; III The Air-Raid; IV The Duplication of Mr. Hearty; V The Gathering of the Bands; VI Mr. Gupperduck's Mishap; VII The Courting of the Rev. Andrew MacFie; VIII The Chapel Conversazione; IX The Letting of Number Six; X The Downfall of Mr. Jabez Stiffson; XI The Camouflaging of Mr. Gupperduck; XII The Tragedy of Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino; XIII The Return of Charlie Dixon; XIV Mr. Hearty Yields; XV A Billeting Adventure; XVI Millie's Wedding.

**Ch I:** Bindle and wife Mrs. (Lizzie) Bindle, married 19 years, live in Fenton Street. Mrs. B answers ad in *The Gospel Sentinel* ("Christian home wanted by single gentleman... Apply Lonely"). Lodger = Mr. Josiah Gupperduck: small, thin, large round spectacles, three wisps of hair, short brown beard, red nose, ears like sign-boards; lecturer for Society for Suppression of Atheism; plays accordion; "sower of the seed"; calls Bindle a blasphemer. Bindle's pipe conflict; "lodger" monologue; Horace Gaze anecdote (telegram/key). Bindle drinks at The Yellow Ostrich; blue-and-white jug with crimson butterfly. Bindle "special" constable, all-clear bugle joke. Mr. Hearty (Alfred Hearty, greengrocer, married Mrs. Bindle's sister Martha; wheezes, breath trouble; Mrs. Hearty = Martha). Bindle says "'Ow the injiarubber ostridge..." Gupperduck "Mr. Wot-a-duck"/"sounds like a patent mackintosh." Bindle's "Ole Buttercup"/Bindle-chapel jokes.

**Ch II (Downing Street):** Bindle hired by Messrs. Empsom & Daley, cartage; with pale weedy youth Tippitt (cigarette on lip). Van from John Smith & Co., Merton, with carved-oak furniture for Mr. Llewellyn John, 110 Downing Street. Bindle fills roof with lamp-black (bought at Wimbledon oil-shop, "Startin' a minstrel troupe"), watering-can with lamp-black, pea-puffer. Hidden contents: suffragettes ("Black and White Raiders," ~20 women, white dresses, coloured sashes). Bindle tells Inspector (police) plan. Tippitt knocked down by doors. Women smeared black, herded into Whitehall; refused taxis. Chief-Inspector Gunny of Scotland Yard praises Bindle; Deputy-Commissioner gives cigar. Bindle ends at The Feathers.

**Ch III (Air-raid):** Bindle at Heartys' during raid; Mr. Gupperduck and Mr. Hearty hide in potato-cellar; Bindle drops scales to scare them; Mrs. Bindle faints; Millie Hearty (niece, sweetheart of Charlie Dixon, soldier in 110th Service Battalion, London Regiment) loyal; "You are the only Uncle Joe I've got."

**Ch IV:** Mrs. Bindle sulks ("You've never been a real husband"). Bindle visits Dick Little (Chelsea flat), with brother Tom Little and Guggers (Captain, Gordons, Oxford, stammers "gug-gug"; Bindle calls him "Spit-and-Speak"). They plan a rag to advertise Hearty's third shop in Putney High Street. Next day: six duplicate "Mr. Hearty"s (alibis) appear; Smith (right-hand man) hides in cellar; Billy Nips errand boy. Hearty threatens to charge them.

**Ch V:** Donkey procession with boards ("Alfred Hearty, Napoleon of Greengrocers," "Hearty's Two-Shilling Pineapple," "Eat Hearty's Filberts, Oh! Gilbert," "Pineapple Alf," camel: "I've got the hump through not buying Hearty's vegetables"). Rival brass bands (Pull for the Shore Sailor; Onward Christian Soldiers; Shall We Gather at the River; Gospel Bells; Last Noel) swarm shop; drummers Ted and Striker; leader Charlie; Mrs. Bindle: "That Bindle's done this."

**Ch VI:** Mr. Gupperduck beaten after addressing Peace meeting in Hyde Park (wounded soldiers); black eye, cheek bruised; two supporters, man with sandy beard (Peter, cap too big) and little man with long beard (Mr. Wayskin, lost trousers). Bindle fed him brandy; Mrs. Bindle: "he's temperance." Bindle: "I'll camelflage 'im" (in Ch XI). Atheists in Regent's Park anecdote.

**Ch VII:** Rev. Andrew MacFie (Scottish, "Mrs. Beendle", "Proveedence") courts Millie; Rev. Mr. Sopley retiring from Alton Road Chapel; Lady Knob-Kerrick arranges MacFie as pastor (Temperance Fete at Barton Bridge fiasco, lemonade mixed with spirits by Bindle; "a lemon-and-a-mac" drink). Miss Sarah MacFie (sister). Bindle: "It's like an 'ippopotamus a-givin' the glad-eye to a canary." Bindle's Sunday dinners; Bindle's Uriah/David anecdote; Millie "I understood."

**Ch VIII (Conversazione):** Chapel school-room; scriptural texts; Mr. Pain, Mr. & Mrs. Withers, Mr. Tuddenham & Mr. Muskett, Miss Torkington (Bindle: "So shall ye all likewise perish"), Mr. & Mrs. Gash, Mr. Hippitt, Mrs. Muspratt; servant Alice. Glee party sings "The Glad Eye." Lady Knob-Kerrick presents Sopley's purse of £50, illuminated address, silver-mounted hot-water bottle; footman John; companion Miss Strint. Mrs. Gash? A woman (Nancy Dane, Passchendaele Pierrette, "Nancy" disguise by Dick Little/Private Dane) claims to be MacFie's wife; police whistle blown by John → raid panic. MacFie denies (scarlet woman). Magistrate dismisses summonses.

**Ch IX (Letting of Number Six):** Bindle temporarily caretaker at Fulham Square Mansions for friend Charlie Hart (wife ill). Mrs. Sedge (Mrs. Hart's mother, Royal Richard gin). Tenants: No. 7 choleric ex-Indian civil servant (Bindle "'Oly Joe"); No. 8 maid "Queenie"; No. 12 Fluffles (Pekinese); No. 15 maid. Number Six let to Mr. Jabez Stiffson (3½ guineas/week; canary Oscar; thermos) and Miss Cissie Boye (actress in revue "Kiss Me Quick" at Regent Theatre) — double letting. Bindle's special's uniform.

**Ch X (Downfall of Mr. Stiffson):** Morning: Cissie in bath-room scene; Stiffson in pink bath-robe; Mrs. Stiffson (tall, grey, "Jabez!") arrives; porridge bowl dropped on Stiffson's head by Mrs. Stiffson; she has hysterics; locked in lift by Bindle/Number Seven. Stiffson flees.

**Ch XI (Camouflaging of Guppy):** Bindle at The Yellow Ostrich with Ginger (Ging), Wilkes (coughs), Huggles; Ginger's Pincher Nobbs grudge; Bindle's stories about Llewellyn John and King George V. Bindle reports Guppy assaulted in Putney Heath peace meeting; Mrs. Bindle nurses; Bindle: "I'll camelflage 'im."

**Ch XII (Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino):** Bindle becomes waiter at Napolini's, Regent Street, via Scratcher (Cockney). Italian waiter Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino (fierce moustache, hostile), Bindle calls him "Kayser"; Scratcher; Herr Smith (Mr. James Smith, chief superintendent, Dundreary whiskers) hit in solar-plexus. Tolmenicino arrested as spy under Defence of the Realm Act; Vine Street. Bindle's curried prawns, champagne in hot water, "caille en casserole" incident.

**Ch XIII (Return of Charlie Dixon):** Charlie home 10 days. Millie + Charlie dine at Universal Cafe (champagne "Number 68"); Bindle pushes marriage before Tuesday; Charlie: "Uncle Joe." Millie: "I wish I could give every girl an Uncle Joe."

**Ch XIV (Mr. Hearty Yields):** Bindle confronts Hearty; threat of lady (Ratty; "Six-an'-Eightpence") revealing Hearty's secret; Hearty consents; wedding set for Tuesday (next Toosday).

**Ch XV (Billeting Adventure):** Bindle, Ginger, Huggles, Wilkes on Harridge's Stores pantechnicon to Lady Knob-Kerrick's, The Poplars, Putney Hill; 16 bedsteads billeting; butler Mr. Wilton; housekeeper Mrs. Marlings; footman John/"Calves"; sergeant with 15 soldiers; Lady Knob-Kerrick: "Why are you not in the army?" Bindle: "various veins." Bust of Sir Benjamin Biggs; Huggles' hat on bust. Lady Knob-Kerrick: close account, sue Harridge's.

**Ch XVI (Millie's Wedding):** Chapel wedding by Sopley; Mrs. Bindle's green bonnet; Bindle's cigar; Mr. Hearty's hat under carriage; Millie to Charlie; Mr. Dixon (John Dixon, hurly-burly, drinks whisky, "Splendid!") and Mrs. Dixon (gentle; "you must be a very good man"). Bindle's speech; the Pink 'Un Bible joke; taxi away to Putney Bridge. "THE END" of Bindle.

## BOOK 2: A TRAITOR'S WOOING (Headon Hill; Ward Lock, 1909)

**Ch I (Two Villains and the Heroine):** Brabazon House ball, London season. Travers Nugent (middle-aged, fair moustache, close-set blue eyes, lives on wits; Jermyn Street flat; cottage "The Hut" in Ottermouth, Devon; "avuncular oof-bird" uncle) and Bhagwan Singh, Maharajah of Sindkhote (turban, jewels) pursue Violet Maynard (daughter of Montague Maynard, Birmingham screw-manufacturer, Harborne/Park Lane). Violet refused Maharajah's proposal. Plot: kidnap Violet via Leslie Chermside (ex-24th Lancers, penniless, in Sindkhote as drill-instructor, debts bought by Jew Levi Levison). Payment £20,000. Steam yacht *Cobra* (turbine, chartered; Portland/Weymouth).

**Ch II (A Screw Loose):** Ottermouth, South Devon; club; Vernon Mallory (retired Foreign Office, pale ascetic) and Reggie (Lieut. Reginald Beauchamp, RN destroyer, Plymouth; mother Mrs. Beauchamp, Lorne Villas). Chermside meets Levison at the marsh (old estuary, Flagstaff Hill). Levison threatens writs; meeting set for next night, 10 pm, marsh. Chermside decides to renounce plot, honestly in love with Violet.

**Ch III (Presage of Storm):** Manor House (rented by Maynards). Aunt Sarah Dymmock (tiny, sharp, great-aunt, fortune). Louise Aubin (French maid) and onion-seller Pierre Legros (ex-sweetheart). Nugent warned: Chermside will not go on. Maharajah's rebuff recounted.

**Ch IV (Nugent Moves a Pawn):** Nugent's manservant Sinnett (sphinx-like). Nugent tells Levison to press Chermside. Sinnett to fetch Pierre Legros.

**Ch V (Under the Searchlight):** Enid Mallory (Vernon's daughter, Reggie's sweetheart; calls him "Reggie", he calls her "Pussy"). Hear scream at marsh "ambush" (glade of dwarf oaks). Footsteps; searchlight from cruiser *Terrible* shows Chermside.

**Ch VI (Cry from the Train):** Chermside tells Nugent he's out. Picnic at marsh grassy patch (Nugent recommended). Train passenger shouts "the face in the pool" (Violet's words).

**Ch VII (Face in the Pool):** Mallory finds body of Levison in pool under railway embankment; Reggie notes throat cut from ear to ear.

**Ch VIII (Intercepted):** Louise meets Nugent on road, tells him Pierre suspect; Nugent says Chermside was meeting Levison.

**Ch IX (Inquisitive Foreman):** Lazarus Lowch (nosy foreman of inquest, hides behind hedge). Inquest: Leslie admits business; Reggie reveals scream evidence.

**Ch X (Lure of Love):** Chermside and Violet in rose garden, declare love.

**Ch XI (Peering Eyes):** Louise sees them; tells Nugent; Pierre Legros hears; Nugent threatens him. Mallory suspects Vernon's onion-seller; old man with no hair seen by Legros.

**Ch XII (Cobra's Sailing Orders):** Nugent visits Weymouth, meets Captain Simon Brant (deformed, cruel, "Simon Brant"), Bully Cheeseman (mate). Signal: "Advance" telegram; blue then green light off Coldbrook Chine.

**Ch XIII (Fool's Paradise Lost):** Maynard quizzes Leslie re money; Aunt Sarah transfers securities £250,000 to Leslie. Sail with Violet, Aunt Sarah. Nugent summons Leslie to club.

**Ch XIV (Creaking Stair):** Nugent says Levison's murder will be pinned on Leslie; Louise's suspicion; plan flight on Cobra. Leslie notices creak on stair; billiard-room: Mallory, General Kruse, Lowch overheard (ambiguity).

**Ch XV (Council of Three):** Enid and Reggie engaged; Mallory's study; "The Bootlace Man" tramp seen at window selling laces.

**Ch XVI (Barbed Shafts):** Dinner at Manor; Louise tells Violet; Nugent to Violet; Leslie tells Violet "I had appointment... didn't murder him." Violet: "Is that all you have to say to me?"

**Ch XVII ("The Bootlace Man"):** Enid explores The Hut; locked in stone grotto by Bill Tuke ("The Bootlace Man").

**Ch XVIII (Trap is Set):** Nugent tells Violet Leslie fled; meets her at Ottermouth road at 11 pm.

**Ch XIX (Sleeping Snake):** Cobra sails; Brant hires stewardess Nettle Jimpson (draper's assistant, Grigg & Winter's, Weymouth; sweetheart Ned Parsons, petty officer on destroyer *Snipe*). Violet is taken aboard.

**Ch XX (Blue Light and Green):** Leslie hides at The Hut; Nugent sends him off with Tuke; signals blue/green flares.

**Ch XXI (Trap Closes):** Violet taken to launch; Nugent leaves her; Tuke "wait would be long."

**Ch XXII (Shadow of Horror):** Leslie climbs aboard, struggles, knocked out; Violet on Cobra.

**Ch XXIII (In the Stone Grotto):** Enid in grotto with Pierre Legros; escape through roof.

**Ch XXIV (In the Toils):** Brant reveals destination Sindkhote; Violet confined; Nettle befriends.

**Ch XXV (Last Chance Fails):** Nettle finds Leslie chained in lower-deck black hole; Brant refuses Plymouth.

**Ch XXVI (Enid Is "Mixed Up"):** Lowch tells Mallory Enid went into The Hut; Mallory and Enid phone exchange.

**Ch XXVII (Pursuit):** Enid phones Reggie at Devonport (12.30 am); Snipe chases Cobra, Ned Parsons recognises Nettle.

**Ch XXVIII (Travers Nugent Pays):** Sergeant Bruce; Mallory charges Nugent; Pierre confesses killing Levison; Pierre stabs Nugent and then himself.

**Ch XXIX (Sting of the Nettle):** Nettle drops cinders into Cobra's engine; engines stop; Brant threatens Nettle; Snipe boards.

**Ch XXX (Aftermath of Storm):** Maynard, Mallory, Reggie dine; Chermside pardoned; Maynard buys Grigg & Winter for Nettle; Lowch engaged to Louise. "THE END."
